**Strategic Philosophy:** *“One Global Supply-Integrity & Supplier-Qualification Core, Certified Regional Supplier-Integration Profiles”*

The failure mode in rapid nearshoring consolidation is treating supervisory divergence, quality-management heterogeneity, language/legal separation, and entrenched local-plant culture as “communication formatting”: copying the group quality manual into a Mexico/Morocco/Vietnam box without process-integrated quality licensing, signing 90-day local-plant-manager retention contracts that hide upstream group-control dependencies, allowing procurement to interpret every local capacity reserve as group opportunism, and delaying core-specification correlation until a 2026 customer or customs audit forces emergency migration—resulting in specification divergence, unverified quality-integration claims, customs/enforcement action, supplier exodus, or permanent customer churn to incumbent competitors.

The correct model is a **modulated global supplier-integration platform**: a standardized global supply-integrity backbone (non-negotiable quality-risk taxonomy, integration-commitment registry, specification-parity firewall, geo-supply traceability, crisis protocol) packaged into **region- and culture-specific “Supplier Integration Profiles”**—each with its own quality-certification pipeline, local-plant-trust covenant, specification-correlation tradition, contract/governance instrument profile, and embedded regional governance team.

---

### 1. The Four-Layer Global Supplier-Integration Architecture

| Layer | Scope | Function | Integrity / Governance Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1: Global Supply-Integrity & Anti-Fragmentation Core** | Global (all supplier jurisdictions / all supply tiers; core components, sub-assembly, logistics, digital quality/systems) | Non-negotiable backbone: **unified quality-compliance taxonomy** (Tier **S—Systemic-Strategic** / core electronics components, regulated/customs-critical inputs, final-assembly lines, regulatory/customs reporting / Tier **C—Critical-Functional** / sub-assembly, packaging, spec-integration nodes, logistics hubs / Tier **R—Replaceable-Standard** / internal analytics, HR, non-production tools) with defined residency, certification-baseline, and customs/regulatory requirements; **separated commitment-component registry** tracking every supplier-integration agreement as **Migration Investment (quality-system correlation / line-certification)** + **Local Capacity Reservation (plant/line/local buffer/inventory)** + **Group Specification Subscription Commitment (Base unified quality/spec platform + Swing/Protection for local continuity)** + **Transition Window / Buffer (months)**; **dual-region verification rule**—a “qualified supplier region” means full quality-parity correlation, customs/license verification, supply-flow isolation verification, spec-system access correlation, and upstream dependency mapping completed—not a group logo on a local supplier portal; **fragmentation firewall** preventing unqualified (T3) regional-supply claims, “paper dual-certification” status, or hidden upstream foreign-node dependencies (e.g., Moroccan-certified component routed through Vietnamese logistics hub without customs/quality approval); **geo-supply traceability mandate**—every component flow, quality audit, specification version, and logistics movement mapped to jurisdiction cluster and hidden upstream dependency flagged; **global crisis-escalation protocol** for quality-divergence shock, customs audit failure, local-plant collapse, or certification-revocation risk. | Every jurisdiction-region has a visible, audited **Supplier Integration Qualification Status**: **B0 (Unqualified—contract/planning)**, **B1 (Certification in Progress—pilot line permitted)**, **B2 (Qualified—Quality & Spec Integrated)**, **B3 (Qualified—Volume/Migration Committed)**. No Tier S strategic supply workflow may migrate to B0/B1 region without L3 pilot-exception and board-level audit trail. Registry open to procurement, engineering, quality, customs/legal, and customer audit. |
| **L2: Regional Supplier-Integration & Trust Profile** | Cultural-market / regulatory / management-trust clusters: **Profile S — Sovereignty-Positive / Regulatory-First** (high government/customs-trust, local-plant celebration, certification-nationalism); **Profile F — Specification-Parity / Continuity Focused** (enterprise fear of quality/delivery disruption); **Profile C — Procurement-Trust-Deficit / Transparency-Demanding** (vendor/group suspicion, autonomy demand, open-book covenant); **Profile E — Emerging / Unified-Quality-Platform Qualification** (new group digital quality backbone, capacity-constrained local partners, milestone-gated promotion) | Defines **quality-certification boundary** (6-month fast-track for digitally-equivalent spec replication vs. 18–24 month full system correlation); **local-plant-management-trust covenant** (radical autonomy vs. co-certification vs. retention-board covenant vs. milestone-co-investment); **contract/governance instrument profile** (local-plant preservation + customs-covenant vs. spec-guarantee + unified-dashboard covenant vs. open-book termination-right + board-autonomy agreement vs. staged qualification-agreement); **geo-supply / group-dependency exposure label** (Regulatory-First / Continuity-First / Concentration-Risk / Emerging-Platform); **procurement-communication covenant** (how capacity, control, technology, and continuity are explained to local boards, plant managers, customs authorities, and customers); and **finance-bridge structure** (how long-term local-capacity and technology-commitment is translated to treasury-acceptable terms without hidden extraction). | Published in **“Supplier Integration Playbooks”**: Profile S = High-Regulatory-Trust / Local-Plant Priority; Profile F = Continuity-First / Spec-Parity Guarantee; Profile C = Transparency-First / Autonomy & Audit Covenant; Profile E = Phased-Qualification / Co-Investment Pipeline. No global procurement director may impose Profile C’s open-book termination terms onto Profile S’s co-certification partnership, or apply Profile E’s unverified platform onto Profile F’s production component stream, without Regional Integration Council approval. |
| **L3: Calibration, Integration Pipeline & Pilot Audit** | Cluster-adapted supplier cohorts, production lines, and regional supply nodes | Tiered pipeline: **Foundation** (global taxonomy active, B-status registry live, upstream geo-logistics dependency mapped, fragmentation firewall tested); **Quality Certification & System Correlation** (customs/regulatory notification; quality-system feature-parity study across components/assembly/logistics/regulatory filing; supply-flow isolation and inventory-buffer verification; local-plant governance integration; language/localization and legal-jurisdiction audit); **Pilot Manufacturing / Shadow Production** (limited-component or limited-line “shadow integration” cohort with parallel quality monitoring—spec-access logs, quality-reporting accuracy benchmarks, delivery-correlation tracking, plant-management retention metrics, logistics-flow audit sampling, supplier-churn-risk signal); and **Conflict-Integration Drill** (simulated 2026 customs/quality audit—testing migration-speed, spec-parity activation, strategic-transition-window drawdown, local-certification enforcement, and crisis-communication protocol). | Migration budget allocated by **supply-systemic exposure and strategic-criticality tier** (Tier S strategic/customs-critical > Tier C functional/logistics > Tier R internal/non-customer)—not by contract value alone. Pilot-line production mandatory before B1→B2 promotion; no “emergency promotion” of B0 region to production-status integration without L4 crisis authorization and audit trail. |
| **L4: Governance, Local Plant Economics & Crisis Credibility** | Local / Cluster / Supplier-Entity | **Local Supplier-Integration Director** (embedded regional—language-native, manufacturing-culture and customs-tradition literate, not remote HQ “global sourcing manager”); **regional quality / customs partner** (independent local certification body for quality/customs compliance; local legal entity for contract/license jurisdiction); **localized board/plant-transparency portal** (region-language explanation of spec-flow map, logistics-covenant, quality-parity status, cost-component breakdown, plant-management retention terms, transition timeline); **real-time integration-integrity monitoring** (certification-tracking, spec-divergence alerts, plant-management retention risk signals, supplier-churn-risk signal, logistics-flow audit, industry/customs tracking); and **crisis-escalation pathway** (Profile S: government/customs-stakeholder protocol; Profile F: spec-parity emergency release + procurement/customer advisory notification; Profile C: board-autonomy / audit-termination activation + open-book disclosure; Profile E: pilot-scale promotion + co-investment release; global: procurement commitment-release + board-level supply-security disclosure). | Every qualification-stage promotion, management-retention restructuring, transition-window adjustment, technology-source change, and spec-divergence alert is traceable to L3 evidence and L2 labeling. Playbooks standardized globally but executed by locally embedded supplier-integration teams—not centralized group-sourcing managers applying uniform “supplier onboarding templates.” |

---

### 2. Regional Supplier-Integration Profiles: The Three Divergent Trust Regimes

The past failure—“copy the group spec sheet into a local box”—manifests when a “Mexican USMCA-certified supplier” retains only branding while components are routed through unverified foreign nodes, when Vietnamese assembly lines promise “identical group quality products” but local testing protocols and delivery-logistics integrations are deferred 14 months, when Moroccan boards are handed an opaque “group technology fee” with no upstream logistics disclosure, or when the unified quality platform is promoted to “production-ready” without 18-month system correlation—resulting in customs enforcement, quality failure, supplier flight, or customer defect.

| Dimension | **Profile S: Sovereignty-Positive / Regulatory & Customs-First (Mexico)** | **Profile F: Specification-Parity / Continuity Focused (Vietnam)** | **Profile C: Transparency-Deficit / Autonomy & Audit (Morocco)** | **Profile E: Emerging / Unified-Quality-Platform Qualification (Group Backbone)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cultural / Procurement & Board Lens** | High regulatory/customs nationalism; USMCA/customs authorities expect local-certification sovereignty; local plant management expects capacity-covenant and audit rights; procurement seeks **customs-certification, local-contract preservation, partnership covenant**. Fears “group extraction” of local production/data. | High continuity anxiety; procurement/engineering fears **spec-divergence, delivery-delay, quality-dashboard fragmentation** relative to legacy East Asian hub. Seeks **continuity guarantees, spec-parity timelines, logistics-protection**. Communication indirect/face-saving. | Francophone/Arabophone; EU/customs-aligned (CE/ISO); local board deeply suspicious of “foreign group imperialism” and hidden logistics/control dependencies; procurement seeks **radical cost/transparency, contract termination rights, board-autonomy covenant, local legal recourse**. | The group is deploying a **unified digital quality/spec backbone** that does not yet exist at full qualification for any jurisdiction. Local boards and customs authorities are skeptical of migrating strategic supply to an unproven system. Seeks **phased proof, co-investment clarity, milestone-gated promotion**, not immediate full replacement. |
| **Manufacturing / Customs Context** | Nearshore US market; USMCA rules of origin/customs documentation; strong union/labor-law framework; Spanish/English bilingual with deep regional dialects; relationship-driven culture (**confianza/personalismo**); quality traditions may prioritize throughput and flexibility over granular documentation traceability. | Manufacturing-mature but **new to this manufacturer’s ecosystem**; indirect/high-context communication; collective responsibility norms may conflict with individual audit-traceability demands; logistics/delivery commitments interpreted as relational rather than contractual; Vietnamese/English language barriers. | Civil-law jurisdiction; French-origin documentation likely; Arabic/French contract law; EU-market quality alignment demands rigorous documentation; distinct customs protocols (EU-Morocco agreements); board culture values formal legal clarity and autonomy. | Global taxonomy not yet correlated to regional line-level testing, logistics nodes, or customs-documentation pipelines. No B2/B3 promotion permitted without pilot-line evidence. |
| **Quality / Certification Boundary** | 6–12 month **customs-correlation + local-certification** pipeline; emphasis on USMCA documentation integration, labor-compliance correlation, local testing-protocol equivalence—not full system replacement. | 12–18 month **spec-parity correlation**; shadow production required to verify electronic component tolerances, assembly precision, testing protocols match legacy hub; delivery-logistics integration tested separately. | 18–24 month **full system correlation** with open-book audit gates; European-aligned quality documentation required at every stage; termination rights retained until B2 verified. | Milestone-gated: pilot line (B1) → audit-correlation (B2) → volume commitment (B3). No production migration to B0/B1 regions. |
| **Local-Plant Trust Covenant** | **Co-certification partnership**: local plant retains contract sovereignty; customs-covenant signed jointly; capacity reservation treated as local strategic asset, not group extraction pool. | **Continuity-covenant + shadow-integration**: delivery buffers protected; spec-parity dashboard shared in real-time; management retained with transparent milestone bonuses, not hidden dependency contracts. | **Autonomy + open-book audit covenant**: full cost/spec/logistics disclosure; local board retains termination rights; audit partner embedded locally; no hidden upstream logistics routing permitted. | **Staged co-investment agreement**: group funds pilot-line correlation; local partner funds capacity; promotion to next B-status requires mutual audit sign-off. |
| **Contract / Governance Instrument** | Local-plant preservation + customs-integration covenant; group subscription with local swing-protection; bilingual contract (Spanish/English). | Spec-guarantee + unified quality-dashboard covenant + delivery-buffer protection; written confirmation loops required for every audit finding. | Open-book termination-right + board-autonomy agreement + local legal-entity contract (French/Arabic); audit-release gates embedded. | Staged qualification-agreement; co-investment pipeline; pilot-only contract until B2. |
| **Communication / Trust Protocol** | **Personal / high-context**: face-to-face onboarding mandatory; local director must build *confianza* before audit; family/business network acknowledgment; direct confrontation avoided—use collaborative problem-solving framing. | **Indirect / face-saving**: documented confirmation loops after every meeting; spec-divergence never labeled as “failure” in group forums—use “correlation gap” language; written verification required; avoid public criticism of plant management. | **Formal / contract-first**: all commitments documented in French (and Arabic where required); legal recourse clarity emphasized; transparency portal must show upstream logistics map; direct negotiation permitted but requires formal minutes. | **Evidence-only**: no “production-ready” marketing until B2 audit trail published; milestone reports in local language; board transparency mandatory. |
| **Geo-Supply / Dependency Exposure** | **Regulatory-Aligned / Nearshore Concentration**: USMCA dependency high; hidden upstream dependency risk if Mexican-certified parts rely on unverified non-USMCA inputs. | **Continuity-Risk / Emerging Integration**: dependency risk if Vietnamese lines rely on unverified legacy-East-Asian nodes for critical specs; logistics nodes must be mapped. | **Concentration-Risk / European-Aligned**: dependency risk if Moroccan supply is routed through foreign logistics without customs-quality correlation; EU data/quality rules may apply. | **Platform-Risk**: dependency risk if unified backbone routes regional quality data through unverified foreign nodes. |

---

### 3. The Implementation Pipeline: From Audit Failure to Certified Integration

**The Catalyst:** Early audits revealed misunderstandings about electronic-component specifications and delivery commitments—classic symptoms of treating integration as “communication formatting” rather than process-embedded certification.

**L3 Pipeline Execution:**

**Phase I — Foundation & Fragmentation Audit (Months 1–3)**
- Activate global taxonomy: classify all nearshored components into Tier S (core electronics/customs-critical), Tier C (sub-assembly/logistics), Tier R (internal/non-customer).
- Launch **B-status registry** for Mexico, Vietnam, Morocco, and the Group Backbone: all begin at **B0**.
- **Upstream dependency mapping**: Identify hidden logistics nodes (e.g., Vietnamese sub-assembly using legacy East Asian testing equipment; Moroccan components routed through Spanish logistics without quality correlation; Mexican inputs with non-USMCA origin risk). Flag all in geo-traceability system.
- **Fragmentation firewall test**: Verify that no supplier region is presented to customers/customs as “fully integrated” before B2 audit.

**Phase II — Certification & System Correlation (Months 4–15, region-staggered)**

| Region / Profile | Certification Focus | Pilot Design |
|---|---|---|
| **Mexico (Profile S)** | USMCA/customs documentation correlation; local labor-law integration; bilingual quality-document equivalence; local testing-protocol mapping to group spec. | **Limited-line pilot** (e.g., one product family) with local plant co-management; customs documentation tested on actual shipment; capacity reservation covenant signed. |
| **Vietnam (Profile F)** | Spec-parity study against legacy East Asian hub: component tolerances, assembly precision, functional testing protocols, packaging integrity; delivery-logistics correlation; indirect-communication verification loops installed. | **Shadow production cohort**: parallel production of identical SKU at Vietnamese and legacy hub; quality logs compared in real-time without public “failure” labeling; delivery timelines monitored against buffer covenant. |
| **Morocco (Profile C)** | Full system correlation to EU-aligned/ISO quality documentation; open-book audit of cost/spec/logistics; contract autonomy verification; French/Arabic documentation audit; termination-right mechanism tested. | **Audit-gated pilot**: production permitted only after open-book disclosure signed; independent local quality partner audits every lot; board-level autonomy verified contractually before B1 promotion. |
| **Group Backbone (Profile E)** | No B1 promotion permitted for strategic (Tier S) workflows until pilot-line correlation completed in at least two regions. | Pilot-line deployment in lowest-risk Tier C category first; milestone-report published to all regional boards before any strategic migration claim. |

**Phase III — Pilot Manufacturing & Conflict-Integration Drill (Months 12–24)**
- **Shadow integration cohorts** run with parallel quality monitoring: spec-access logs, delivery-correlation benchmarks, logistics-flow audit sampling, plant-management retention tracking.
- **Conflict-Integration Drill (Simulated 2026 Audit)**:
  - *Mexico*: Customs authority challenges USMCA origin documentation—test transition-window drawdown, local-certification enforcement, government-stakeholder protocol.
  - *Vietnam*: Spec-divergence detected in shadow cohort—test spec-parity emergency release, procurement advisory notification, face-saving communication protocol to retain management trust.
  - *Morocco*: Board activates termination-right due to hidden upstream logistics dependency—test open-book disclosure, audit-termination activation, local legal recourse.
  - *Group*: Treasury attempts to accelerate B0→B2 promotion for cost savings—test crisis-authority and board-level security disclosure.

**Phase IV — Qualification Promotion & Volume Migration (Months 18–30)**
- B0 → B1 (pilot permitted): Requires L3 evidence of certification start and dependency mapping.
- B1 → B2 (Quality & Spec Integrated): Requires pilot-line correlation evidence, audit-partner sign-off, local-management covenant verified, no hidden upstream dependency.
- B2 → B3 (Volume/Customer Migration Committed): Requires sustained quality metrics, delivery-correlation, workforce retention stability, and crisis-drill pass.
- **No “emergency promotion”** permitted without L4 crisis authorization and full audit trail.

---

### 4. Governance, Local Economics & Crisis Credibility (L4)

| Element | Mexico (Profile S) | Vietnam (Profile F) | Morocco (Profile C) | Group Backbone (Profile E) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Local Integration Director** | Bilingual (Spanish/English); USMCA/customs expert; embedded in plant, not remote HQ; builds *confianza* through personal presence. | High-context communication expert; quality engineer fluent in Vietnamese technical norms; avoids direct public criticism of management. | Francophone legal/quality expert; embedded board-level; formal contract-minutes culture; independent from group sourcing. | Global integration lead; milestone-evidence only; no regional authority without local co-signature. |
| **Regional Certification Partner** | Independent Mexican customs/quality certification body; local labor-law auditor. | Independent Vietnamese testing/correlation partner; logistics audit specialist. | Independent Moroccan/European-aligned audit firm; local legal entity for contract enforcement

run.userPrompt:
Following the tariff realignments and export-control expansions of 2025, a consumer-electronics manufacturer is shifting part of its supply base from its historical hub in East Asia to new suppliers in Mexico, Morocco, and Vietnam. The new supplier relationships involve unfamiliar business customs, different quality-management traditions, and workforces with distinct communication styles, and early audits reveal misunderstandings about specifications and delivery commitments.

Develop an approach for onboarding and integrating new suppliers from three culturally distinct regions after a rapid nearshoring shift, ensuring quality, trust, and reliable communication.

| **Quality / Certification Boundary** | 6–12 month **customs-correlation + local-certification** pipeline; emphasis on USMCA documentation integration, labor-compliance correlation, local testing-protocol equivalence—not full system replacement. | 12–18 month **spec-parity correlation**; shadow production required to verify electronic component tolerances, assembly precision, testing protocols match legacy hub; delivery-logistics integration tested separately. | 18–24 month **full system correlation** with open-book audit gates; European-aligned quality documentation required at every stage; termination rights retained until B2 verified. | Milestone-gated: pilot line (B1) → audit-correlation (B2) → volume commitment (B3). No production migration to B0/B1 regions. |
| **Local-Plant Trust Covenant** | **Co-certification partnership**: local plant retains contract sovereignty; customs-covenant signed jointly; capacity reservation treated as local strategic asset, not group extraction pool. | **Continuity-covenant + shadow-integration**: delivery buffers protected; spec-parity dashboard shared in real-time; management retained with transparent milestone bonuses, not hidden dependency contracts. | **Autonomy + open-book audit covenant**: full cost/spec/logistics disclosure; local board retains termination rights; audit partner embedded locally; no hidden upstream logistics routing permitted. | **Staged co-investment agreement**: group funds pilot-line correlation; local partner funds capacity; promotion to next B-status requires mutual audit sign-off. |
| **Contract / Governance Instrument** | Local-plant preservation + customs-integration covenant; group subscription with local swing-protection; bilingual contract (Spanish/English). | Spec-guarantee + unified quality-dashboard covenant + delivery-buffer protection; written confirmation loops required for every audit finding. | Open-book termination-right + board-autonomy agreement + local legal-entity contract (French/Arabic); audit-release gates embedded. | Staged qualification-agreement; co-investment pipeline; pilot-only contract until B2. |
| **Communication / Trust Protocol** | **Personal / high-context**: face-to-face onboarding mandatory; local director must build *confianza* before audit; family/business network acknowledgment; direct confrontation avoided—use collaborative problem-solving framing. | **Indirect / face-saving**: documented confirmation loops after every meeting; spec-divergence never labeled as “failure” in group forums—use “correlation gap” language; written verification required; avoid public criticism of plant management. | **Formal / contract-first**: all commitments documented in French (and Arabic where required); legal recourse clarity emphasized; transparency portal must show upstream logistics map; direct negotiation permitted but requires formal minutes. | **Evidence-only**: no “production-ready” marketing until B2 audit trail published; milestone reports in local language; board transparency mandatory. |
| **Geo-Supply / Dependency Exposure** | **Regulatory-Aligned / Nearshore Concentration**: USMCA dependency high; hidden upstream dependency risk if Mexican-certified parts rely on unverified non-USMCA inputs. | **Continuity-Risk / Emerging Integration**: dependency risk if Vietnamese lines rely on unverified legacy-East-Asian nodes for critical specs; logistics nodes must be mapped. | **Concentration-Risk / European-Aligned**: dependency risk if Moroccan supply is routed through foreign logistics without customs-quality correlation; EU data/quality rules may apply. | **Platform-Risk**: dependency risk if unified backbone routes regional quality data through unverified foreign nodes. |

---

### 3. The Implementation Pipeline: From Audit Failure to Certified Integration

**The Catalyst:** Early audits revealed misunderstandings about electronic-component specifications and delivery commitments—classic symptoms of treating integration as “communication formatting” rather than process-embedded certification.

**L3 Pipeline Execution:**

**Phase I — Foundation & Fragmentation Audit (Months 1–3)**
- Activate global taxonomy: classify all nearshored components into Tier S (core electronics/customs-critical), Tier C (sub-assembly/logistics), Tier R (internal/non-customer).
- Launch **B-status registry** for Mexico, Vietnam, Morocco, and the Group Backbone: all begin at **B0**.
- **Upstream dependency mapping**: Identify hidden logistics nodes (e.g., Vietnamese sub-assembly using legacy East Asian testing equipment; Moroccan components routed through Spanish logistics without quality correlation; Mexican inputs with non-USMCA origin risk). Flag all in geo-traceability system.
- **Fragmentation firewall test**: Verify that no supplier region is presented to customers/customs as “fully integrated” before B2 audit.

**Phase II — Certification & System Correlation (Months 4–15, region-staggered)**

| Region / Profile | Certification Focus | Pilot Design |
|---|---|---|
| **Mexico (Profile S)** | USMCA/customs documentation correlation; local labor-law integration; bilingual quality-document equivalence; local testing-protocol mapping to group spec. | **Limited-line pilot** (e.g., one product family) with local plant co-management; customs documentation tested on actual shipment; capacity reservation covenant signed. |
| **Vietnam (Profile F)** | Spec-parity study against legacy East Asian hub: component tolerances, assembly precision, functional testing protocols, packaging integrity; delivery-logistics correlation; indirect-communication verification loops installed. | **Shadow production cohort**: parallel production of identical SKU at Vietnamese and legacy hub; quality logs compared in real-time without public “failure” labeling; delivery timelines monitored against buffer covenant. |
| **Morocco (Profile C)** | Full system correlation to EU-aligned/ISO quality documentation; open-book audit of cost/spec/logistics; contract autonomy verification; French/Arabic documentation audit; termination-right mechanism tested. | **Audit-gated pilot**: production permitted only after open-book disclosure signed; independent local quality partner audits every lot; board-level autonomy verified contractually before B1 promotion. |
| **Group Backbone (Profile E)** | No B1 promotion permitted for strategic (Tier S) workflows until pilot-line correlation completed in at least two regions. | Pilot-line deployment in lowest-risk Tier C category first; milestone-report published to all regional boards before any strategic migration claim. |

**Phase III — Pilot Manufacturing & Conflict-Integration Drill (Months 12–24)**
- **Shadow integration cohorts** run with parallel quality monitoring: spec-access logs, delivery-correlation benchmarks, logistics-flow audit sampling, plant-management retention tracking.
- **Conflict-Integration Drill (Simulated 2026 Audit)**:
  - *Mexico*: Customs authority challenges USMCA origin documentation—test transition-window drawdown, local-certification enforcement, government-stakeholder protocol.
  - *Vietnam*: Spec-divergence detected in shadow cohort—test spec-parity emergency release, procurement advisory notification, face-saving communication protocol to retain management trust.
  - *Morocco*: Board activates termination-right due to hidden upstream logistics dependency—test open-book disclosure, audit-termination activation, local legal recourse.
  - *Group*: Treasury attempts to accelerate B0→B2 promotion for cost savings—test crisis-authority and board-level security disclosure.

**Phase IV — Qualification Promotion & Volume Migration (Months 18–30)**
- B0 → B1 (pilot permitted): Requires L3 evidence of certification start and dependency mapping.
- B1 → B2 (Quality & Spec Integrated): Requires pilot-line correlation evidence, audit-partner sign-off, local-management covenant verified, no hidden upstream dependency.
- B2 → B3 (Volume/Customer Migration Committed): Requires sustained quality metrics, delivery-correlation, workforce retention stability, and crisis-drill pass.
- **No “emergency promotion”** permitted without L4 crisis authorization and full audit trail.
